g.text: Guest side, Go built for wasip1

g.title: The result holds the seed, fault list, trace and a hash over every host call. replay, shrink and verify all start from the seed, and run -check runs each seed twice and stops at the first host call that differs.

A small Go program built with the stock toolchain that drives the cluster. It imports sim for Always, Eventually and Sometimes properties, Put and Get history records, sim.Budget and sim.Listen. Outside the simulator, sim.Listen and sim.Dial call the standard net package.
Each node package is built with GOOS=wasip1. No forked runtime and no source rewriting. Code that needs cgo cannot build, and mmap or flock code needs a built-in or hand-written shim.
Compiles each guest once, after adding a call counter to every function in the wasm (instrument.go), and caches the result in .seedfall/cache. Every node start or restart is a fresh module instance.

Runs exactly one node at a time. It picks the earliest fault, restart or wake-up, breaks ties with the seed and jumps virtual time forward. The clock, random_get (ChaCha8) and poll_oneoff are the three WASI calls it implements.

One file system per node with a page cache: Sync makes writes durable and a crash keeps only durable data. Options add torn writes, reordered page writeback, strict_dirs, fsync EIO, full disks, lost writes and bit flips.
Ordered TCP streams with seeded latency and UDP datagrams that can reorder, drop or duplicate. Faults are rules on one direction of a link, so one-way partitions fall out of the same code.

After the run, Put and Get records are checked for linearizability with Porcupine against a sequential model. With the list-append model, an in-house Elle-style checker looks for isolation anomalies in sim.Txn histories.
